title: Tensor product with a separably closed field has a unique minimal prime
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Then the ring $K\otimes_k L$ has a unique minimal prime; consequently $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k L)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: Let $p$ be the characteristic exponent of $k$ and let $\bar k$ be a perfect closure of $k$ (the elements of an algebraic closure of $k$ some $p^m$-th power of which lies in $k$); $\bar k/k$ is purely inseparable. $\bar k$ is algebraically closed: if $\alpha$ is algebraic over $\bar k$, it is algebraic over $k$, and some $\alpha^{p^m}$ is separable over $k$, so $k(\alpha^{p^m})/k$ is a finite separable extension, trivial because $k$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]; thus $\alpha^{p^m}\in k$ and $\alpha\in\bar k$. Put $R=K\otimes_k\bar k$ and $S=L\otimes_k\bar k$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] applied to the $k$-schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(L)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kL)$, the maps $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\to\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(L)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}((K\otimes_kL)\otimes_k\bar k)\to\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kL)$ are homeomorphisms, and $(K\otimes_kL)\otimes_k\bar k=R\otimes_{\bar k}S$. A homeomorphism carries minimal primes (the generic points of irreducible components) bijectively, so it suffices to show that $R\otimes_{\bar k}S$ has a unique minimal prime, over the algebraically closed field $\bar k$.

Each of $R$, $S$ has exactly one prime, since its spectrum is homeomorphic to the point $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, resp. $\operatorname{Spec}(L)$ (Step 1); so its nilradical is its unique (maximal) prime and its reduction $R_{\mathrm{red}}$, $S_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a field, in particular a domain. The kernel of $R\otimes_{\bar k}S\to R_{\mathrm{red}}\otimes_{\bar k}S_{\mathrm{red}}$ is generated by the elements $n\otimes1$ and $1\otimes n'$ with $n,n'$ nilpotent, so it is a nil ideal and the two spectra are the same; replace $R$, $S$ by $R_{\mathrm{red}}$, $S_{\mathrm{red}}$, which are domains. Since $\bar k$ is perfect, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] makes $R\otimes_{\bar k}S$ reduced.

$R\otimes_{\bar k}S\neq0$ (a tensor product of nonzero $\bar k$-vector spaces) and it is reduced (Step 2), so it has a unique minimal prime as soon as it is a domain, i.e. has no nonzero zero-divisor. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-type-limit], if it had a nonzero zero-divisor there would be finitely generated $\bar k$-subalgebras $R'\subset R$, $S'\subset S$ with a nonzero zero-divisor in $R'\otimes_{\bar k}S'$. Subalgebras of the domains $R$, $S$ are domains, so it suffices to show: for finitely generated $\bar k$-domains $R'$, $S'$, the ring $T=R'\otimes_{\bar k}S'$ is a domain.

Let $R'$, $S'$ be finitely generated $\bar k$-domains and $T=R'\otimes_{\bar k}S'$. $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ is irreducible since $R'$ is a domain. $R'\to T$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] because $S'$ is a free $\bar k$-module and $-\otimes_{R'}T=-\otimes_{\bar k}S'$. It is of finite presentation: $S'\cong\bar k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] ($\bar k$ is Noetherian), hence $T\cong R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R'$ (a closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$, which is of finite type over $\bar k$), [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] gives $\bar k\cong\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R'/\mathfrak m$, so the fibre $T\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak m)\cong S'\otimes_{\bar k}\kappa(\mathfrak m)\cong S'$, whose spectrum is irreducible because $S'$ is a domain. The maximal ideals are dense in $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$: by the in-particular clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal], every basic open $D(f)$ containing a prime $\mathfrak p$ contains a maximal ideal. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fibres-irreducible] applies to $R'\to T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(T)$ is irreducible.

$T$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] ($R'$, $S'$ are domains, $\bar k$ is perfect), nonzero, and has irreducible spectrum (Step 4), so its nilradical $0$ is its unique minimal prime: $T$ is a domain. By Step 3, $R\otimes_{\bar k}S$ is a domain, so $0$ is its unique minimal prime; by Steps 2 and 1 (same spectrum after reduction, bijection on minimal primes), $K\otimes_kL$ has a unique minimal prime. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kL)$ is the closure of that generic point, hence irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components], and an irreducible space is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].
